## `ComposableTuringIDModels.jl`

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
- The proof of concept, a library of parts over `Turing.jl`
- Three kinds of part. An infection model, an observation model, and
  prior models nested in the slots of both
- Parts carry their own priors
- A model definition does not know about the data. One definition
  simulates and fits
- Adding a new application means defining only the novel parts
- Every part is a plain struct with one method of `as_turing_model`

## The parts are structs

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
```julia
struct IDModel{I, O} <: AbstractComposableModel
    infection_model::I   # process → I_t
    observation_model::O # I_t → y_t
end

struct AR{D, I, P, E, F} <: AbstractLatentModel
    damp::D
    init::I
    p::P
    ϵ_t::E              # an innovation slot
    transform::F
end

struct MA{C, Q, E} <: AbstractLatentModel
    θ::C
    q::Q
    ϵ_t::E
end

struct DiffLatentModel{M, P} <: AbstractLatentModel
    model::M
    init::P
    d::Int
end
```

::: {.attribution}
Struct fields abridged, parameter bounds dropped ·
`src/latent_models/models/{AR,MA}.jl` and
`src/latent_models/modifiers/DiffLatentModel.jl`, `main` at `011169f`
:::
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
- A part is a plain struct. The type tree does the bookkeeping
- A slot holds a fixed prior or a whole other part
- Composition is replacing what is in a slot
- A part is identified by the method it implements, not by its place in
  a type tree

::: {.attribution}
`docs/src/design.md:18-20`
:::
:::

## ARIMA(2,1,1)

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
```julia
ar2 = AR(;
  damp = [truncated(Normal(0.2, 0.2), 0, 1),
          truncated(Normal(0.1, 0.05), 0, 1)],
  ϵ_t = HierarchicalNormal(std = HalfNormal(0.1)))

ma1 = MA(;
  θ = [truncated(Normal(0.0, 0.2), -1, 1)],
  ϵ_t = HierarchicalNormal(std = HalfNormal(0.1)))

# the AR's innovation slot now holds the MA process
arma21 = @set ar2.ϵ_t = ma1
arima211 = DiffLatentModel(arma21, Normal(0, 0.2); d = 1)
```

::: {.attribution}
Run against `main` at `011169f` for this talk · `@set` is
`Accessors.jl`, not ours · Keywords track `main`. The paper's artefact
pins an earlier release, where these were `damp_priors`, `θ_priors` and
`std_prior`
:::
:::
::: {.column width="42%"}
![](../figures/composable-arima.png){height="500px" fig-align="center"
fig-alt="MA(1) inside AR(2) inside ARMA inside ARIMA, then Poisson"}
:::

## `as_turing_model`, inside the ARIMA call

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="56%"}
```julia
mdl = as_turing_model(arima211, 100)

# DiffLatentModel draws its init, then descends:
@model function as_turing_model(model::DiffLatentModel, n::Int)
    latent_init ~ as_turing_submodel(model.init, model.d; prefix = true)
    diff_latent ~ as_turing_submodel(model.model, n - model.d)
    return _combine_diff(latent_init, diff_latent, model.d)
end

# model.model is arma21: an AR whose ϵ_t slot holds the MA
# AR draws its damp and init, then descends again:
#   ϵ_t ~ as_turing_submodel(model.ϵ_t, n - 1)
```

::: {.attribution}
`src/latent_models/modifiers/DiffLatentModel.jl:61-68` and
`src/latent_models/models/AR.jl:99-115`, `main` at `011169f`, comments
added · 61 `as_turing_model` definitions across 45 files in `src/`,
counted 2026-08-12
:::
:::
::: {.column width="44%"}
- Every part implements `as_turing_model`; nothing else is needed
- A part that holds another part draws it as a submodel, so the call
  descends through the slots
- `AR` was never told that `MA` exists
- `mdl` is a `DynamicPPL.Model`; it simulates and fits from one
  definition

::: {.attribution}
`as_turing_model(model::AR, n)` is the last recursion shown; it passes
its `ϵ_t` slot to `as_turing_submodel`, which resolves the `MA`
:::
:::
::::

## `as_turing_submodel`

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="56%"}
```julia
# a component writes its parameter once
damp ~ as_turing_submodel(model.damp, p; prefix = true)

# what is passed to the call picks the method
as_turing_submodel(m, args...; prefix = false) =
    to_submodel(as_turing_model(m, args...), prefix)

as_turing_submodel(d::Distribution, ::ModelShape;
    prefix = false) = d
```

::: {.attribution}
Two of the three `as_turing_submodel` methods,
`src/base/priors.jl:65-82`, reformatted to fit and with the `::Bool`
annotations dropped. The third takes a vector of priors · The call line
is `src/base/priors.jl:25` · The `AR` example is
`src/latent_models/models/AR.jl:40-43`
:::
:::
::: {.column width="44%"}
- A call takes a fixed prior or a whole process
- A `Distribution` draws one scalar. A process draws a path of length
  `n`
- `AR(damp = Normal(...))` is a constant coefficient,
  `AR(damp = RandomWalk())` a time-varying one
- The component that makes the call is not changed either way
:::
::::
